references.text: The testimony (the tablets of the law) that God was to give Moses was to be placed in the ark. This verse mentions the testimony that is to be placed in the ark.
Repeats the instruction to place the mercy seat on top of the ark of the testimony in the Most Holy Place.
Describes the testimony as two stone tablets written with God's finger, which were to be placed in the ark.
Fulfillment of the command: Moses put the testimony in the ark and set the mercy seat upon it.
Moses recounts that he placed the new stone tablets in the ark, confirming the practice of keeping the testimony in the ark.
Confirms that the tablets were placed in the ark that Moses had made, just as the Lord had commanded.
Confirms that there was nothing else in the ark except the two stone tablets that Moses placed there at Horeb.
The Epistle to the Hebrews describes the ark of the covenant with its mercy seat and contents, including the tablets of the law, as a typological connection to Christ.
Theological elaboration: 30:6 explains the function of the atonement cover as God's meeting place above the testimony.
Complementary description: 26:33 defines its location behind the veil, while 25:21 defines its contents.
